What do I need to keep anonymous and uncensored access to the internet in the event that we really go all 1984? I want to be prepared before it's too late, but I'm a technological novice.
What do I need technologically to keep anonymity and uncensored internet access?

First - realize that there is no such thing. That's your first step.

Secondly . here's a list of things you can try to maximize your privacy:

Hosted/Web Services

  • Email: If you must use a hosted email service - use Proton Mail or Tutanota. They have web mail and mobile apps. It's just mail. These services encrypt your mail on disk and give you options to encrypt email to senders - even senders who don't understand GPG or know how to open such things.

  • If you must use a calendar, use a local calendar. Sunbird is a decent enough application on the desktop.

  • For search, use DuckDuckGo, Startpage or Searx.

  • Use Bleep or Tox for internet messaging. Both are end-to-end encrypted and decentralized. Tox is open source, Bleep is not. These have desktop and mobile clients.

Browsers

  • Firefox on Android and on Linux (or Windows if you must) should be the only browser you use. The only time I'm not using Firefox, I'm using the TorBrowser, with the same extensions:
    • NoScript - whitelist javascript domains you trust
    • CookieMonster - whitelist cookie domains you trust
    • Random Agest Spoofer - Randomized your User Agent
    • Smart Referrer - change what "referrer" is sent to websites you visit
    • HTTPSEverywhere

Mobile

  • On Android use Orbot for Tor, and OrFox for browsing.

  • On Firefox mobile and OrFox, you can use NoScript. There's a version for mobile called "NoScript Anywhere". You can also use HTTPSEverywhere. And Random Agent Spoofer and Smart Referrer.

  • Use Signal for SMS, it's end to end encrypted.

  • Leave wifi and bluetooth off on your phone unless you need it and connecting to things you trust.

Local (Desktop) Security

  • Store your files locally on a USB key. Encrypt the key with Truecrypt/Veracrypt rather than Dropbox or Evernote

  • Do whole disk encryption on laptops with LUKS (linux) or Truecrypt/Veracrypt (windows). Do full disk encryption on your phone. Password protect your phone, don't use your fingerprint.

Passwords

  • Use Keepass. Create unique passwords for EVERYTHING. Have Keepass auto-generate complex, alpha-numeric-symbolic passwords with caps and lower case, 15-25 characters. If you want to be SUPER secure, append a word (or have 2-3 on hand) that are ONLY in your memory. Every password you use starts with this word. For instance. If the word is GOAT. Use Keepass to generate password. Keepass will generate GG)#$goiu345i1oog!.4 So your password will be GOATGG)#$goiu345i1oog!.4 This way your password for everything is something you know PLUS something you have, and that something you have is unique to every site. You can also use Keepass to save insane answers to security questions. "Who is my 1st Grade Teacher?" Answer: "BrownStickyNaziPants" Things like that. Use a keyfile+password to open the keepass database. The keyfile should have it's extension renamed to something obscure. Instead of pwsafe.key you name the files big-tits.jpg The database shouldn't be a .kdb file either. Make it something obscure too. Back up the database periodically on a usb key, or something that's not connected to the internet.

  • Use two-factor auth for services when you can. Prefer QR codes over SMS messages. If you use SMS, only use this on services that you don't mind can identify you. Call your Wireless ISP - create security questions that MUST be answered to change anything on your account.

Misc Tips

  • Try to do most of your browsing over Tor or a VPN. Or both.

  • Do not post sensitive information, or financial info, when browsing over either - if possible.

  • Minimize mobile usage and minimize how often you have your phone on you. Prefer search maps directions through Tor rather than GPS turn by turn navigation.

  • Avoid cloud services when you can use something local.

  • Shop local when applicable, use cash.

  • Use Guerilla Mail, or 10 Minute Mail or AirMail when you need to use an email on a temporary basis for services that won't identify you. For instance, ProtonMail requires you to have another email address to sign up. I used Air Mail (as they block Guerilla and 10 Minute Mail) to sign up. Create these accounts using Tor so the email hosters don't know your IP either.

  • Have a burner/track phone. Use this phone for things that require a phone number that you don't want to give out your number to. Try to pay off the pre-pay phone with Gift Cards or prepay credit cards you buy with cash. Some places ask you for your name and home address to verify the card somehow, but NOT everywhere checks this info. Always test if you can put fake data in those fields. Save that data to your keepass so you remember where you lied and how.

Best thing you can do, honestly? Is just use cash and stay off the web when possible.

If you were talking LastPass, I would say you're far more likely to be hacked. LastPass has had numerous (successful) attempts at breaching their security one way or another. The Heartbeat SSL bug affects syncing of the database over SSL. Recently their "autofill" mechansim in browser plugins was exploitable (and fixed).

LastPass does 2 things KeePass does not.

First - LastPass is cloud hosted. This means your database, and everyone else's database is hosted in the same place. It's a honeypot that's every hacker's wet dream. What's more - is they are a US company and can be compelled by the US government to give the government access, and they can be gagged from ever talking about it. People say "well LastPass encrypts it before sending, and it sends over SSL - so Last Pass can't even get into your DB". SSL/Heartbleed, as noted, had bugs. There's been other bugs sense. As for local encryption - this brings me to my next point.

LastPass's big benefit is all it's browser extensions rather than mere stand aloneapps. These apps are meant to make autofill easy and far more advanced than KeePasses auto-fill. As an author of malware, you don't need to break the encryption of the file if you can exploit an extension that has access to an open database in the browser itself.

Keepass (or it's Android and Linux variants) is a stand-alone, separate application. It does not integrate with your browser out of the box. It does not store your shit in the cloud. You have a local database. That database is, itself, encrypted.

Can Keepass be exploited? Sure. There's ways (as i mentioned) to obfuscate it a bit. You can name your database with a file extension that betrays what it actually is, for instance - making it difficult for malware to know where it is.

I keep my database on a USB key that's also encrypted with Truecrypt (with a lot of other stuff that I use daily at home and work) So there's never a file just sitting on my computer waiting to around to be gotten into. I back up my Truecrypt volumes to another larger USB drive at home, periodically.

The chances of someone getting into it, aren't 0. But it's slim. I would have to be specifically targeted by a hacker who knew who i was and what my usage case it. I could imagine some malware could get me - if it ran on Linux and was intelligent enough to go undetected by me, AND could circumvent my various safeguards and obfuscations. I mean..that'd take some fucking doing. That'd be very specific malware for a very specific usage case. At this point, that level of malware is getting close to the "state sponsored" level of complexity. Not quite there, bu almost.

What is MORE insecure is having similar passwords everywhere. When Tumblr, Myspace, Yahoo, and a number of other places got hacked - people were scripting out hacks to get into Netflix, Github, Teamviewer - using username/pw combinations from the first grouping of hacks. They weren't hacking Teamviewer...they were logging in with creds that people re-use.

If you want to make KeePass even more secure - you can come up with your own two-factor solution. Use keepass to generate complicated usernames and passwords for you, but append a word or a rotating set of words, to the password. Do Not Store that word anywhere. Not even in keepass.

So for example your username would be "stohgiu4j6yh908rth" and your password would be "goatseoignergiounrt". But keepass would only have ""eoignergiounrt" (minus "goats" at the front")

So lets challenge it to do something useful: Parsing logging data. (e.g. Microsoft log files or any kind of tracing file, telemetry data)

Lets assume that:

  • I have 100 tracing files, 80 of them are from perfect working PC's and 20 of the are from failing PC's.
  • I have no clue how the log files are constructed.
  • I have no clue what to search for.
  • The trace files are 100,000 lines of traces each.
  • The trace files are not nicely constructed so there is no line with a "==> Start method 1" and another line that ends with "<== End method 1"

What I want it to do is:

  • The AI should tell me that a log file I give is from a failing PC or a working PC. (I have a few hundreds of these PC's to scan for)
  • The AI should tell me what is different in that failing log file. Help me to understand what is causing the issue.
  • The AI should be able to classify what the issue is and how many times it occurs on that PC.
